The items can be indexed using for example N integers. All ndarrays are homogeneous : every item takes up the same size block of memory, and all blocks are interpreted in exactly the same way. How each item in the array is to be interpreted is specified by a separate data-type object , one of which is associated with every array. In addition to basic types (integers, floats, etc. ), the data type objects can also represent data structures. An item extracted from an array, e.g. , by indexing, is represented by a Python object whose type is one of the array scalar types built in NumPy. The array scalars allow easy manipulation of also more complicated arrangements of data. Arrow guide # Adding arrow patches to plots. Arrows are often used to annotate plots. This tutorial shows how to plot arrows that behave differently when the data limits on a plot are changed. In general, points on a plot can either be fixed in "data space" or "display space". Something plotted in data space moves when the data limits are altered - an example would be the points in a scatter plot. Something plotted in display space stays static when data limits are altered - an example would be a figure title or the axis labels. Arrows consist of a head (and possibly a tail) and a stem drawn between a start point and end point, called 'anchor points' from now on. pages.text: Art and Architecture Tour | Tate Modern Enjoy a guided tour through Tate Modern, exploring the building and its collections Discover Tate Modern through its architecture and art. Explore the building’s history and transformation from power station to art gallery, alongside significant works that have helped shape Tate’s collection of international modern and contemporary art. Bringing the building and collection into focus, this tour offers a fresh perspective on the gallery and the art within it. These one-hour tours are limited to just 20 guests, keeping the experience intimate and accessible. Explore the building and selected artworks in a small-group setting, with time to take a closer look. Led by a Tate Expert Guide with years of experience, these tours are suitable for first time visitors as well as those wanting a guided experience. Recommended for all ages 8 years and over. Accessibility All Tate Modern entrances are step-free. You can enter via the Turbine Hall and into the Natalie Bell Building on Holland Street, or into the Blavatnik Building on Sumner street. There are lifts to every floor of the Blavatnik and Natalie Bell buildings. Alternatively you can take the stairs. Fully accessible toilets are located on every floor on the concourses. A quiet room is available to use in the Natalie Bell Building on Level 4. Ear defenders can be borrowed from the Ticket desks. pages.text: Art Chit Chats | Tate Britain Discover new ways of looking at artworks with your family Art Chit Chats invite children and their carers to respond to open-ended questions about artworks within Tate’s collection. Delivered by Tate staff during school holidays and half-term, sessions last between 10 - 20 mins and encourage conversations about artworks in a relaxed environment. No prior knowledge of the artist or artwork is needed—just curiosity! Suitable for children aged 4+, Art Chit Chats are a fun activity for the whole family designed to spark the imagination! Accessibility Tate Britain's step-free entrance is on Atterbury Street. It has automatic sliding doors and there is a ramp down to the entrance with central handrails. Accessible, standard and Changing Places toilets are located on the Lower floor. Ear defenders can be borrowed from the ticket desk on the Lower floor. To help plan your visit to Tate Britain, have a look at our visual story . It includes photographs and information about what you can expect from a visit to the gallery. Admission Membership Members are always free Become a Member About Artists in the 1930s confronted a world on fire. When the United States economy went into freefall on “Black Tuesday,” October 29, 1929, shockwaves of financial panic radiated as banks failed, factories shuttered, and workers were fired en masse. "Art Front: Prints and Politics in the United States, 1929 – 1945" spotlights a generation of U.S. artists forged in the crucibles of the Great Depression, Roosevelt’s New Deal, and the threat of fascism. Tracing how these pressures pushed artists out of the studio and into the streets as part of organized struggle, the exhibition uncovers the power and potential of printmaking for responding to the unprecedented crises of the moment. pages.text: Art of Magnificence: Philip the Good and Isabella of Portugal | Cleveland Museum of Art Art of Magnificence Tags For: Art of Magnificence Special Exhibition Philip the Good and Isabella of Portugal Sunday, October 24, 2027–Sunday, February 6, 2028 Location: 003 Special Exhibition Hall The Kelvin and Eleanor Smith Foundation Exhibition Hall Ticket Info Coming Soon View Featured Art Sunday, October 24, 2027–Sunday, February 6, 2028 Location: 003 Special Exhibition Hall The Kelvin and Eleanor Smith Foundation Exhibition Hall Ticket Info Coming Soon View Featured Art Jump to: Share Back to Top About The Exhibition The Cleveland Museum of Art, in partnership with the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Dijon in Dijon, France, presents a major exhibition exploring the life, legacy, and cultural impact of Duke Philip the Good (1396–1467) of Burgundy and Isabella of Portugal (1397–1471), one of the most influential ruling couples of 1400s Europe. Bringing together exceptional loans from leading international museums and collections, the exhibition features some of the most celebrated works of art created during a period of extraordinary political, economic, and artistic achievement. Under Philip the Good, the Burgundian Netherlands emerged as one of Europe’s most prosperous and culturally sophisticated regions, rivaling the great centers of the Italian Renaissance, such as Florence. Through paintings, manuscripts, sculpture, tapestries, jewelry, and luxury objects, the exhibition examines how art, ceremony, diplomacy, and courtly magnificence were employed. pages.text: Art thief who targeted Edgar Davids is sentenced to jail Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Art thief jailed after targeting Edgar Davids 10 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Metropolitan Police A friend of ex-Premier League star Edgar Davids who stole his £188,000 modern art collection has been jailed in her absence for 28 months. Nabila Habiby, 39, sent multiple works of art belonging to Davids to auction, after he had trusted her to put his possessions into storage during a house move. Ther former Spurs midfielder believed the works were secured in a storage facility in Enfield, north London and only became suspicious when a luxury watch went missing. During sentencing on Wednesday at Wood Green Crown Court, Judge Alexander Jacobs said Habiby, who had failed to turn up for four previous court hearings, had a "streak of dishonesty throughout her relationships with others". He also said she "appears to be someone who thinks nothing of breaching the trust placed in her by people who consider them to be friends". A warrant has been issued for for her arrest and she is now expected to be brought back from Belgium to the UK to serve her sentence. The court heard Habiby, a former wealth manager, "abused her position as a friend to essentially steal". pages.description: NASA is targeting the first Artemis lunar landing in early 2028. After launching the crew aboard the Orion spacecraft, they will transfer to a commercial lunar lander for transport to the surface of the Moon. Lander readiness will determine which provider will safely carry them to the surface and back to Orion in lunar orbit before the crew returns home aboard Orion—splashing down safely in the Pacific Ocean.
